newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer after choppy session.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly firmer after a choppy session with the market barely clinging to its modest gains after being lower for much of the day.

Most-active July settled 0.10 cent firmer at 118.20 cents a lb, traded 118.70 to 116.70 cents. Spot June went out 0.10 cent higher at 118.60 cents, with September, set to become most active, also ending 0.10 cent higher at 116.20 cents.
Volume was moderate at an estimated 13,000 lots.
"The market popped up just a bit because of bad weather conditions in Chile," Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said.
Heavy snow has already affected some gold-mining operations, but there were concerns that shipments from copper mines may become delayed, Raptopoulos said.

Meanwhile news on Monday that South Korea's Finance Ministry has begun probing the country's big rise in LME futures and options trading, failed to unnerve the market in any significant way, dealers said.
Despite the earlier losses and choppiness, the LME backwardation firmed Monday to $137/$147, up from $110/$120 at Friday's close.
COMEX stocks on Monday rose 300 short tons to 49,930 short tons. LME stocks rose 225 tonnes to 121,775 tonnes.
